title: "xLAM-60k"

---

{{< include /_setup.qmd >}}

[xLAM-function-calling-60k](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Salesforce/xlam-function-calling-60k)
is Salesforce's dataset of single-turn tool calls: 60,000 rows generated by their APIGen pipeline,
each answer checked by executing it. Each row is a user **query**, the **tools** on offer (name,
description, typed parameters) and the **gold answer**, the list of calls that satisfies the query:

```json
{
  "query": "Where can I find live giveaways for beta access and games?",
  "tools": [{"name": "live_giveaways_by_type",
             "description": "Retrieve live giveaways from the GamerPower API based on the specified type.",
             "parameters": {"type": {"description": "The type of giveaways to retrieve (e.g., game, loot, beta).",
                                     "type": "str", "default": "game"}}}],
  "answers": [{"name": "live_giveaways_by_type", "arguments": {"type": "beta"}},
              {"name": "live_giveaways_by_type", "arguments": {"type": "game"}}]
}
```

The model sees the tools and the query through Qwen3.5's chat template, with thinking off, and must
answer with the JSON list and nothing around it. Answers range from one call to several calls to
different tools, or the same tool called in parallel with different values.

::: {.column-margin}
xLAM is gated (accept its terms on the Hub) and CC-BY-4.0. The dataset statistics on this page come
from [the dataset card](https://github.com/joaomigueloliveira/qwen-function-calling-distillation/blob/main/docs/DATASET.md),
since the site's build can't read the gated rows.
:::

## The splits

The data is split into `{python} n(splits["train"])` training rows,
`{python} n(splits["validation"])` for validation and `{python} n(splits["test"])` for test.
APIGen generated many queries per tool, so the same sentence recurs with different values ("the
factorial of 7", "of 10"). Rows are therefore **grouped by their normalised query** and whole groups go
to one split, so no query appears in two.

Tools are still shared by construction: test asks the student to fill new values into tools it has seen.
So **xLAM's test measures in-distribution tool calling**, and a second dataset,
[BFCL](bfcl.qmd), measures tools it has never seen.

Validation chooses checkpoints and settings; test is run once, for the checkpoint chosen, to
produce the numbers reported ([how methods are compared](../evaluation/comparing.qmd)).

::: {.column-margin}
[ADR 0001](../decisions/0001-train-validation-test-split.html): the split and the rule that test
only produces official numbers.
:::

## Problems found, and what was done

The data is clean in structure: every answer parses and calls an offered tool. The problems are in
the content:

| Problem | Found | What was done |
|---|---|---|
| Exact duplicate rows | 375 | collapsed to one copy, before splitting |
| Same query and tools, different gold answers | 21 rows | 20 removed from train: no model can be right on both |
| Code instead of a value (`"math.pi / 2"` for a float) | 224 rows | 213 removed from train: it teaches copying text, not computing |
| Train gold answer equal to a validation or test answer | 1,831 rows | removed from train: it would reward memorising answers |
| Optional arguments written at their default | 7.7% of rows | kept; scored by [lenient exact](../evaluation/metrics.qmd) |

Validation and test keep every row as published, so the numbers stay comparable with other xLAM
results. And the gold answers themselves turned out not to be always right: that is the
[label audit](audit.qmd).

::: {.column-margin}
Each finding and the decision it led to:
[the dataset card](https://github.com/joaomigueloliveira/qwen-function-calling-distillation/blob/main/docs/DATASET.md).
:::
